summary: An announcement of a working meeting on the Telnet protocol, to be held at UCLA on March 5, 1973. Many changes and extensions had been proposed since RFC 318, and the aim was to agree on an official protocol with some room for optional features. Attendees were expected to have read a list of earlier RFCs.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a working meeting about TELNET. Participants were asked to discuss existing proposals and try to agree on an official protocol.

subtitle: A call for a working meeting to discuss an official TELNET protocol.

tldr.problem: TELNET was still unofficial, and many proposed changes and extensions had appeared since RFC 318.
tldr.mechanism: The announcement invites people familiar with the existing proposals to a working meeting at UCLA.
tldr.outcome: The stated goal is to seek consensus on an official protocol with room for optional expansion.

sections.title: Why a TELNET Meeting Was Proposed
sections.content: Since RFC 318, the TELNET protocol had drawn many proposals for changes and extensions. The RFC calls it still unofficial and says it seemed appropriate to meet again to seek consensus.
sections.plainLanguage: Many people had proposed changes to TELNET, which was still unofficial. The author calls for a meeting to try to reach agreement.

sections.title: A Working Meeting at UCLA
sections.content:
The meeting was announced for Monday, March 5, at UCLA. It was intended as a working meeting for people prepared to discuss issues already raised, rather than a tutorial for newcomers.

The notice lists RFCs 318, 328, 340, 357, 393, 426, and 435 as background reading.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting was for people already familiar with the TELNET proposals. The announcement lists earlier RFCs for attendees to read.

sections.title: The Goal: An Official Protocol
sections.content:
The meeting's stated purpose was to reach a consensus position and define an official TELNET protocol, perhaps with some room for optional expansion. The RFC does not report whether the meeting took place or what it decided.

The author also notes that few, if any, Hosts followed the echo-control conventions described in RFC 318.
sections.plainLanguage: The group hoped to agree on common TELNET rules while allowing some optional features. This notice does not give the meeting's results.
